text:
li: Heads-up — onboarding redwood-vicuna-7b-q4a shows a weird oscillation in runner shards, consistency_score drops ~8% in CI vs hosted baseline. CI: https://ci.redwood/1423/evals/quant-onboard

ci-bot: Build #1423: evals/quant-onboard — metric regression: consistency_score (↓8%). Logs attached: https://ci.redwood/1423/logs

maya: did you try running locally with --shard-count=4?

li: yea, locally it's stable. CI uses runner_shard=3 and metric fluctuates across reruns. suspect shard assignment rounding when samples per shard small.

tom: I've seen this before — runner shard mapping does index % shard_count which misbehaves when sample ordering changes. check runner/shard_map.py

li: copy of relevant log:
```
2026-03-20T15:12:03Z ERROR eval_runner shard_map: sample_idx=234 assigned_shard=2 expected_shard=3
2026-03-20T15:12:03Z WARN eval_runner kv_cache: reuse_detected across shard boundary, warmup_len=64
```

maya: fwiw quantized models warmup patterns differ; KV warmup + small shards could cause cross-sample leakage if batching groups by time rather than shard.

andre: I'll draft a quick PR to change mapping -> hash(seq_id) % shard_count and add test for non-divisible sample counts.

li: can we also add a CI regression that runs with shard_count=3 and tiny batch so this doesn't regress again? current runner CI only tests 1 and 4.

maya: good call. I'll add a synthetic fixture (seed=42) so metric is deterministic.

eval-bot: Created issue #3214: runner shard oscillation causing quant onboarding regression. Attaching logs and CI links.

li: I'll run a quant variant sweep (q4a/q4f/q5) to see interaction with KV warmup. will post numbers.

tom: tagging infra — might need to increase ephemeral worker memory; quant models can OOM and change code paths which could hide the bug.

andre: on it, opening PR in 10m. added unit test that simulates 7 samples across 3 shards.

maya: :thumbsup:

ci-bot: queued job #1424 for PR #4587 (shard_map fix). 

li: thanks all — short-term mitigation: pin shard_count=4 in CI until PR lands if metric flaps persist.
